title: ldap_auth plugin config
description: The `config` object of an enabled `ldap_auth` plugin, generated from ferrum-edge/ferrum-edge openapi.yaml at v0.9.21 (f9915358c8032214f4034a17c28cdf72d14006c3), component LdapAuthConfig and every component it references. Do not edit: run ci/plugin_config_schemas.py. This is Edge's own configuration schema, governed by Edge's support policy (docs/versioning.md); the plugin catalog records when Edge requires it.

LdapAuthConfig.description: Plugin: ldap_auth — LDAP directory authentication with optional AD group filtering. Status codes distinguish failure classes: invalid credentials or unknown user return 401; a user authorized by bind but not in any `required_groups` returns 403; backend/configuration failures (directory unreachable, service-account bind failure, or search RPC error) return 500 rather than 401, so clients are not falsely told their credentials are wrong. When `required_groups` is set without a service account (`service_account_dn`/`service_account_password`), the group-membership search uses an ANONYMOUS bind; group enforcement then only works if the directory permits anonymous reads of group objects, so a service account is recommended. TLS connections (`ldaps://`/STARTTLS) honor the gateway CRL (`FERRUM_TLS_CRL_FILE_PATH`), rejecting revoked server certificates. Every connection/reconnection performs an uncached A+AAAA lookup, screens the complete candidate set and each imminent dial under the active backend egress policy, and retains the configured hostname for TLS/SNI verification. Non-loopback plaintext `ldap://` is rejected unless the development-only `allow_plaintext` override is explicitly enabled. Exactly one authentication mode may be configured; combining `bind_dn_template` with `search_base_dn`/ `search_filter` is rejected. Both modes require a canonical identity attribute, reject ambiguous or duplicate values, and export the authenticated entry's canonical value rather than the presented username: direct bind reads it with a base-scope search on the bound DN, and search-then-bind takes it from the uniquely selected search entry. A returned group entry satisfies `required_groups` through its `group_attribute` values alone whenever the directory returns that attribute; only an omitted `cn` falls back to the entry's own `cn` RDN. DNs and attribute names are validated at admission. `failover_ldap_urls` adds directory endpoints tried in order when one is unreachable or answers busy/unavailable; credential rejections never fail over.

ldap_url.description: LDAP server URL. Use ldaps:// or ldap:// with starttls=true; non-loopback plaintext ldap:// requires the explicit development-only allow_plaintext override. The scheme is matched case-sensitively and the value must carry no leading or trailing whitespace. A hostname is required and an explicit port must be 1-65535 (port 0 can never be dialed). Embedded URL credentials are rejected; a bare '@' with empty userinfo carries none and is accepted. Each connection freshly resolves and policy-screens all A/AAAA candidates while retaining this hostname for TLS/SNI verification. The connection-establishment budget is split across the screened candidates, so a candidate that stalls during TCP or TLS setup, or fails TLS, leaves time to try the next one.

failover_ldap_urls.description: Further directory endpoints (replicas) tried in order after ldap_url, each validated like ldap_url and using the same scheme. A flow moves to the next endpoint only when the current one cannot be reached, its connection or TLS setup fails, an operation fails at the transport level, or it answers busy (51) / unavailable (52); a credential rejection, a group non-membership, or any other directory error is final. Every attempt shares request_timeout_seconds. The replicas join the identity realm digest.

bind_dn_template.description: Direct bind DN template with {username} placeholder. A DN-shaped template (one containing '=') must, with the placeholder substituted, be an RFC 4514 distinguished name; an Active Directory userPrincipalName ({username}@corp.example.com) or down-level (CORP\{username}) template is accepted as-is.

search_base_dn.description: Base DN for search-then-bind user search. Surrounding whitespace is trimmed; a whitespace-only value is rejected, and the value must be an RFC 4514 distinguished name (an unescaped '=' inside a value is refused as a likely missing comma)

search_filter.description: LDAP search filter with {username} placeholder. The value must also parse as an RFC 4515 search filter; a malformed filter is rejected at load rather than failing every request with 500

canonical_identity_attribute.description: Required in both bind modes. Exactly one value from the authenticated entry (the uniquely selected search entry, or a base-scope read of the directly bound DN) becomes the authenticated identity, Consumer mapping key, custom group-filter {username}, and default memberUid value (for example uid or sAMAccountName). Choose the authoritative attribute whose value username-based groups store; mismatches fail closed and never fall back to the presented login. Attribute-name matching is LDAP case-insensitive. The value must be an RFC 4512 attribute description (a name or numeric OID with optional ;options); 1.1 is refused.

service_account_dn.description: DN for the service account used in search-then-bind. Surrounding whitespace is trimmed; a whitespace-only value is rejected. A DN-shaped value (one containing '=') must be an RFC 4514 distinguished name; an Active Directory userPrincipalName or down-level logon name is accepted as-is.

service_account_password.description: Password for the service account. Taken verbatim: it is never trimmed, so a secret with leading or trailing whitespace binds as configured. Only an empty string is rejected

group_base_dn.description: Base DN for group membership search. Surrounding whitespace is trimmed; a whitespace-only value is rejected, and the value must be an RFC 4514 distinguished name

group_filter.description: Group search filter. The value must parse as an RFC 4515 search filter; a malformed filter is rejected at load. When required_groups is non-empty, a custom filter must contain {user_dn} or {username}. {username} is the authenticated canonical identity read from canonical_identity_attribute in both bind modes, never the presented login. Before authorization, every custom-filter match is rechecked against the exact returned group DN with the membership predicate (member, uniqueMember, and memberUid by default; group_member_attribute and group_membership_mode change it) so a static branch cannot fabricate membership.

required_groups.description: LDAP/AD group names the user must belong to (OR logic). Names compare like LDAP caseIgnoreMatch: case-insensitively, ignoring surrounding whitespace and collapsing interior whitespace runs. When the directory returns group_attribute for a group entry, only those values decide; a present non-matching value never falls back to the DN. Only when group_attribute is cn and the directory omits it does the entry's OWN first RDN stand in, and then only a cn-typed component with a matching RFC 4514-decoded value; any other omitted group_attribute fails closed. An entry merely nested under a required group never matches

group_attribute.description: Authoritative attribute containing the group name (for Active Directory prefer the domain-unique sAMAccountName over cn, which may repeat across OUs); returned LDAP attribute names are matched case-insensitively. Must be an RFC 4512 attribute description; 1.1 is refused.

group_member_attribute.description: DN-valued attribute on group entries that lists members, used for the default group search and for the custom-filter membership recheck instead of the built-in member/uniqueMember/memberUid predicate (for example member or a custom appMember). With group_membership_mode ad_in_chain it names the link attribute evaluated transitively (default member); with member_of it names the attribute on the user's entry listing group DNs (default memberOf). Must be an RFC 4512 attribute description.

group_membership_mode.description: member_of finds the required groups under group_base_dn by their group_attribute value and accepts one only when a base-scope equality search on the authenticated user's entry confirms that its group_member_attribute (default memberOf) lists that exact group DN, so DN matching follows the directory schema; it cannot be combined with group_filter. direct proves membership from the group entry's own membership attribute. ad_in_chain (Active Directory only) uses LDAP_MATCHING_RULE_IN_CHAIN (1.2.840.113556.1.4.1941) on group_member_attribute (default member), so a user who is a member through nested groups matches; the directory evaluates the chain under the group search's size and time limits, and custom-filter matches are rechecked with the same in-chain predicate.

starttls.description: Use STARTTLS to upgrade ldap:// connections; invalid with ldaps://

allow_plaintext.description: Development-only override allowing a non-loopback ldap:// endpoint without STARTTLS. Service-account and user passwords then have no transport confidentiality.

connect_timeout_seconds.description: Per-connection DNS resolution, candidate TCP/TLS establishment, and per-operation timeout in seconds; also applied as the server-side LDAP search time limit

request_timeout_seconds.description: Strict wall-clock deadline in seconds for the complete uncached authentication and group-check flow. The effective default is 15 seconds, raised to connect_timeout_seconds when that value is larger.

max_concurrent_requests.description: Maximum concurrent LDAP directory flows per plugin instance, shared by uncached authentications and due cached group re-checks; excess requests fail immediately

cache_ttl_seconds.description: Cache TTL for successful auth results (0 = disabled, maximum 24 hours). A cache hit skips the bind, so a password change or account disablement in the directory takes effect only when the entry expires; values above 900 seconds log that revocation lag at construction. required_groups membership is re-checked separately (group_cache_ttl_seconds).

group_cache_ttl_seconds.description: With required_groups and the cache enabled, the longest a cached authentication is admitted without re-running the group search (0 = every cache hit). A due hit re-checks membership under max_concurrent_requests and request_timeout_seconds; a user no longer in any required group gets 403 and the entry is evicted, and a directory failure returns 500 and keeps the entry. Never extends cache_ttl_seconds.

max_cache_entries.description: Strict maximum entries in the auth result cache (1-1,000,000). At capacity, one existing entry is replaced without a full-cache scan. Cache keys use the exact presented username and password. The same cap bounds the rejected-credential cache and the per-username failure tracker; the tracker never evicts live failure state, so when it is full an untracked username gets 500.

negative_cache_ttl_seconds.description: How long an exact username/password pair the directory rejected (wrong password or unknown user) is answered 401 without contacting the directory (0 = disabled, maximum 300). A different password for the same username is still checked.

max_failed_attempts_per_user.description: After this many consecutive directory credential rejections for one presented username, that username is answered 401 without contacting the directory for failed_attempt_backoff_seconds, even with the correct password (0 = disabled, maximum 1000). This keeps a spray from reaching directory lockout counters; a successful bind resets the count. The count folds the username's case and whitespace, survives a compatible reload of the same plugin config, and is never evicted while live (a full tracker answers an untracked username 500).

failed_attempt_backoff_seconds.description: How long a username stays refused after max_failed_attempts_per_user consecutive failures; also the quiet period after which its failure count starts over.

service_connection_max_age_seconds.description: Reuse one connection bound as the service account, per directory endpoint, for user and group searches for at most this many seconds (0 = a fresh connection per flow). New shared connections are resolved, screened, dialed, and bound exactly like fresh ones; a shared connection that failed at the transport level is retired. End-user binds always use their own connection. Requires service_account_dn and service_account_password.

hide_credentials.description: Remove the verified Authorization: Basic credential from the backend request, including when another mechanism wins a multi-auth chain. Only the Basic scheme this plugin consumes is removed; an Authorization header carrying another scheme reaches the backend unchanged. Set to false only for a legacy backend that explicitly requires the directory password.
